paper.title: MEMRES: A Memory-Augmented Resolver with Confidence Cascade for Agentic Python Dependency Resolution
paper.central_claim: A six-level confidence cascade (session memory, curated compatibility maps/templates, co-occurrence mining, heuristics, then LLM last) with intra-session memory, self-evolving memory (tips/shortcuts), an error-pattern KB, semantic import analysis and Python 2 detection resolves 86.6% (10-run avg) of HG2.9K snippets with Gemma-2 9B vs PLLM's reported 54.7%, with 68.0% resolved without any LLM call.

rationale: 确定性级联为主、会话记忆为辅。仅有Level 1记忆消融(+5.0pp)；基线数字取自原论文，31.9pp增益未分解；设计基于评测集失败分析，无独立测试。

evidence.quote: an agentic system for Python dependency resolution that introduces a multi-level confidence cascade where the LLM serves as the last resort
evidence.support_explanation: Central design: deterministic levels first, LLM last.

evidence.quote: Our analysis of PLLM’s failures reveals deterministic root causes: 33% are SyntaxErrors from Python 2 code run under Python 3, 30% are ImportErrors for known name mismatches
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: PLLM failures on HG2.9K are mostly deterministic; the design is derived from failure analysis of the evaluation benchmark itself.

evidence.quote: Calling an LLM wastes 60 to 120 s per snippet with no benefit for these cases.
evidence.support_explanation: Cost motivation for the cascade.

evidence.quote: We directly compare against the reported 54.7% success rate from the original PLLM paper
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline is a number copied from the original paper (1583/2891), not rerun on the same hardware, model, timeout or success implementation.

evidence.quote: a snippet is successful when all its pip dependencies are installed and the script executes past all import statements without ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError
evidence.support_explanation: Success = install + survive import statements only (inherited from PLLM), not functional correctness.

evidence.quote: Runtime passes (correct dependencies but environmental failures such as missing display servers or hardware) are counted as failures to prevent inflation.
evidence.support_explanation: Conservative counting of environment-dependent snippets; whether PLLM's 54.7% treats them the same way is not stated.

evidence.quote: Memory is fully reset between independent evaluation runs: no state persists across runs, preventing cross-run overfitting.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention scope: within one evaluation batch only; no cross-run or cross-dataset persistence.

evidence.quote: To address fairness, disabling Level 1 simply forces snippets through the remaining deterministic and LLM levels.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 2: full pipeline 2503 (86.6%) vs Level 1 OFF 2357 (81.6%), delta +146 (+5.0 pp). Only ablation table; no ± for the OFF condition.

evidence.quote: Since PLLM evaluates sequentially within a single session, we emulate this by caching solutions proven successful for earlier code blocks to resolve near-duplicate datasets (e.g., identical GitHub forks).
evidence.support_explanation: Level 1 memory exploits near-duplicate snippets (forks) inside the evaluated batch, i.e. the store is built from the test stream.

evidence.quote: Shortcuts are validated with a quick Docker build to prevent compounding errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Execution-based write gate for shortcuts; no gate described for tips.

evidence.quote: (natural language guidelines) and shortcuts (reusable solutions matched via Jaccard similarity over import sets, threshold 0.5)
evidence.support_explanation: Memory has two entry types; tips' content, injection into prompts and effect are not specified or ablated.

evidence.support_explanation: Disclosed mitigation for KB leakage: about 150 entries from PyPI docs/StackOverflow and about 50 from a disjoint held-out dev subset.

evidence.quote: A manual analysis of a random 100-snippet sample from PLLM’s SyntaxError failures reveals that 91% are actually Python 2 code mis-executed under a Python 3 interpreter.
evidence.support_explanation: Python-2 rules (13 indicators) are designed from failures observed on the evaluation benchmark.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On HG2.9K with Gemma-2 9B, the full cascade resolves 86.6% (10-run mean) and a within-batch, Docker-validated memory adds about 5 pp over the same pipeline without it; efficiency is much better than PLLM's published figures.
assessment.author_claim_vs_supported: Superiority over PLLM and attribution to the confidence cascade/self-evolving memory are not isolated: baseline is a copied number and almost all components are unablated.
assessment.note: retained scoped to the Level 1 store-off ablation inside a single batch; no improver-level or cross-run retention; headline gain is mostly static curated knowledge.

G.reason: Concrete, quantified limitation of the nearest system (PLLM 54.7%, deterministic failure causes, LLM wasted) with neighbours named; but the failure analysis is the authors' own sample on the evaluation set, the gap is domain-specific rather than about a changed harness-level learning component, and cross-snippet memory is motivated only by PLLM's sequential evaluation.

M.reason: Cascade ordering (cheap exact levels, LLM last, Docker verification) is coherent and the memory loop (execute -> validated shortcut -> Jaccard reuse) is explicit, but the mechanism explaining the main gain is static curated knowledge; the role of tips/anti-patterns and why self-evolving memory is needed beyond a cache is thin, and no distinguishing predictions against simpler alternatives are made.

X.reason: Main levels, thresholds (Jaccard 0.5), validation by Docker build, run-level reset and sandboxing are stated. Missing: tips content/usage, how anti-pattern stats are consumed, KB self-learning conflict handling, expiry/rollback inside a batch, partial-match hint handling; prompts only summarised.

E.measurement.reason: Full 2890-snippet denominator with failures counted and runtime passes counted as failures, plus 10 runs; but success is import-level only, and the PLLM figure is copied from another paper without confirming identical success/thresholding and infrastructure.

E.causality.reason: Only the Level 1 memory ablation (+5.0 pp) is tabulated and a prose-only co-occurrence ablation; the 31.9 pp gain over PLLM is not decomposed (KB, Python 2 detector, semantic analyzer, cascade vs LLM-first all untested), tips/shortcuts/runtime KB learning are not separated, and no rerun baseline with the same LLM.

E.holdout.reason: Disclosed mitigations (about 50 KB entries from a disjoint dev subset, pre-2020 co-occurrence data, state reset, no HG2.9K-derived KB entries). But the design was motivated by failure analysis on the evaluation benchmark, there is no separate test set, the store is built from the test stream (near-duplicate forks), and only one dataset and one LLM are used.

E.statistics.reason: 10 randomised-order runs with mean +/- std (9.3 snippets) and complete failure counts; effect over PLLM (32 pp) far exceeds noise. No significance test, PLLM comparator is a single reported value, and the ablation lacks a stated run count.

E.cost.reason: LLM calls per snippet, token reduction, median/P90 time, hardware and timeouts reported against PLLM's published figures. Not like-for-like (PLLM from its paper), and manual curation cost of KBs/maps is excluded.
